fields.meta_title: Document Automation Software You Build and Own | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Describe the files you send and receive. Emergent builds document automation that drafts quotes and letters and reads PDFs. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build Document Automation for What You Send and Receive
fields.hero_description: Describe the templates you fill by hand and the PDFs people send you. Emergent builds document automation that drafts from your data and reads every upload into fields.
fields.features_subheading: Six parts, one app. Use the ones your first document needs and add the rest when a second document calls for them.
fields.feature_1:
Templates from the files you already use

Start from a Word or Google Docs file your team sends today. Fields fill where they sit in the text, and the line-item table grows to fit a one-line quote or a forty-line one.
fields.feature_2:
Drafts filled from your own data

Pull values from a submitted form or from any tool with an API, HubSpot deals included. Every finished file is saved as a PDF and linked to the exact record that produced it.
fields.feature_3:
AI reading for PDFs and scans

Read uploaded files into named fields, such as a policy number or an expiry date. Any field the model is unsure of waits for a person to confirm it before the next step runs.
fields.feature_4:
Checks against your thresholds

Compare each value with the limit you set, such as a quote total or a coverage minimum. Anything that fails goes to the named reviewer in Slack or email, with the file attached.
fields.feature_5:
A table row for every document

Write each drafted or received document to a database you own, with the record it came from and who reviewed it. Find a file by client or vendor instead of searching drives.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take anywhere

Export the templates and the rules behind them to your GitHub repository, along with the database. Keep changing them by prompting, or hand the code to your engineers to extend.

fields.tab_content_1:
Turn a client questionnaire into an engagement letter draft

Every answer in Calder Law's intake form fills a field in the engagement letter, such as the matter type and the fee basis. Because this matter is litigation, the draft adds the $5,000 retainer clause. Ana Ruiz, the responsible attorney, reviews it before it goes out, and the signed copy is saved to the matter record.
fields.tab_content_2:
A priced quote the moment a deal reaches Proposal

When the Acme renewal moves to the Proposal stage in HubSpot, its line items are copied into the quote template and the PDF is attached to the deal. That quote, Q-2291, comes to $28,400. Any quote over $25,000 waits for Dev Patel, the sales director, before the rep can send it.
fields.tab_content_3:
Catch an underinsured vendor before the job starts

Vendors upload insurance certificates to Northwind Properties, and the app reads the policy number, expiry date and per-occurrence limit. Ridgeline Roofing's certificate lists $500,000 per occurrence, under its contract's $1,000,000 minimum. The vendor is asked for a new one, and the job stays on hold until one passes.
fields.tab_content_4:
Offer letters that go out once the hiring manager signs off

Moving a candidate to Offer in Lumen Studio's hiring tracker fills the offer letter template from the hiring record. Sam Okafor's letter carries a $96,000 base salary and goes to Mei Chen, the hiring manager, for approval. Sam then signs from a link on a phone, and the signed PDF is filed with the candidate record.

fields.howto_description: Keep last month's files open while you work through these. Each step settles one decision the app needs, and the last one tests those decisions on real requests.
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Decide how incoming files are read
fields.howto_step_1_des: Collect ten recent copies of each document your team sends or receives every week. Mark which parts change and which never do, and note where the changing data lives today. A file with a stable structure and different names and amounts each time is the right place to start.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Take the latest version your lawyers or managers signed off on and replace each changing value with a named field. Keep their wording exactly as it is. Any clause that appears only sometimes gets its own field for now; the next step decides when it appears.
fields.howto_step_3_des: For every optional clause, write the condition that adds it: a multi-year deal gets a price escalator, and a remote hire gets the equipment policy. Plain sentences are enough. A rule nobody can explain to a new hire needs rewriting before it reaches the template.
fields.howto_step_4_des: List the documents people send you and the fields you need from each one. Name the check that matters most, such as a coverage minimum or a missing date. Then mark the fields that never pass without a person, such as a changed bank account.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Not every draft needs a human, and some always do. Set the line, such as quotes over a set amount or any letter going to a new client. Name a second reviewer as well, for the weeks the first one is away.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Choose where finished files are stored
fields.howto_step_6_des: Signed and approved PDFs can go to Google Drive, back to the CRM record, or into the app's own database. Pick one home per document type. Decide too whether rejected drafts are kept beside the approved ones or deleted.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Run a week of real requests
fields.howto_step_7_des: Turn on one document type for one team and let real requests through for a week. Compare every draft with what the team would have written by hand. Adjust the template or the rules by prompting, then add the next document type once the first runs clean.

plan.angle: The top 10 splits document automation into two jobs: assembling documents from templates and rules (Wikipedia, Gavel, Conga, Checkbox) and reading incoming documents into data (Automation Anywhere, Microsoft AI Builder, Conexiom). Each vendor sells one half. This page wins by treating both as one pipeline an operator owns: intake answers and CRM data in, letters and quotes out, uploaded PDFs read into fields and checked against a rule, with every document and decision saved as a row. Real documents named (engagement letter, quote, certificate of insurance, offer letter) and an honest note on where Zapier, Make and n8n fit.
